neet_che_u20_t08_1.working: Dissolving anhydrous CuSO4 is exothermic because the hydration energy is large. So the temperature rises and ΔsolH is negative.

neet_che_u20_t08_2.working: q = 200 g × 4.18 J/g·K × 8.0 K = 6688 J. Moles = 15.95/159.5 = 0.1 mol. ΔH = −6.688 kJ / 0.1 mol ≈ −66.9 kJ/mol (negative because temperature rose).

neet_che_u20_t08_3.working: By Hess's law, ΔH = ΔsolH(anhydrous) − ΔsolH(pentahydrate) = −66.5 − 11.7 = −78.2 kJ/mol.

neet_che_u20_t08_4.working: Pentahydrate dissolution is endothermic (+11.7 kJ/mol), so the temperature falls and A is true. Its ions are already partly hydrated, so the further hydration energy does not exceed the lattice energy. R is therefore false.

neet_che_u20_t08_5.working: Statement I is incorrect: dissolution is exothermic because hydration energy exceeds lattice energy, not the reverse. Statement II is correct: ΔhydH = ΔsolH(anhydrous) − ΔsolH(pentahydrate).
